conclusion: Do not feed PSI into WP710 as a new independent governor. If PSI is admitted later, ingest it as explicit provenance-bound CognitiveEnvelope SignalReadout evidence, then reuse the existing ControlSnapshot -> AdaptiveCompute -> PerceptionComputeBinding -> PerceptionWorkerPolicy authority chain. WP710 remains queue/dispatch planning and may only preserve or shrink the bound perception compute ceiling.
material_findings: Linux PSI is source-supported as experienced CPU/memory/I/O stall pressure with event-trigger capability and per-cgroup availability.
F2 already has a generic measured-signal envelope with UNKNOWN/degraded/hard-limit semantics.
F2 already has a documented invariant that Perception must not create an independent resource governor.

Current WP710 duplicates max_active_workers/max_perception_work_units in its scheduler policy; this is safe only if bound/clamped to the existing PerceptionWorkerPolicy rather than treated as an independent authority.
No external framework/code import is justified at E2.
hypothesis: PSI-derived envelope signals can improve overload discrimination while retaining one resource-governance chain.
counterhypothesis: Existing compute/reserve and CognitiveEnvelope signals are already sufficient; PSI adds noise and complexity without measurable protection or quality gain.
falsifier: Equivalent bounded overload/recovery ablation must show measurable improvement in resource-pressure discrimination or graceful perception degradation with zero control-reserve violations and acceptable overhead; otherwise retire the PSI addition.
next_exact_gate: Before any E5 handoff, bind the latest WP710 scheduler to exact PerceptionWorkerPolicy authority and design/claim a deterministic ablation that compares existing envelope-only behavior versus PSI-augmented envelope behavior without using VPS/runtime credit in this research receipt.
